item.title: The integral $K_0$-ring of the stack of smooth hyperelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.27267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the integral $K_0$-ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr H_g$ of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g\ge2$ over a field of characteristic zero. We show that it is a free abelian group of rank $8g+2$ for even $g$ and $8g+4$ for odd $g$. We use the isotypic decomposition of the $K_0$ of a related $\mu_{g+1}$-gerbe to obtain presentations for both even and odd $g$'s from the standard quotient presentation of $\mathscr H_g$. Thus, our technique differs from the $CH^\bullet(\mathscr H_g)$ computations of Edidin--Fulghesu, Fulghesu--Viviani, Di Lorenzo, and the $K_0(\mathscr M_2)$ computation of Edidin--Hu. Using Pagani's description of the inertia stack of $\mathscr H_g$, we apply Riemann--Roch to interpret the rank of $K_0(\mathscr H_g)$ as the number of inertia components. Finally, we compare the $K_0$ and Chow rings of $\mathscr H_g$ through the gamma-filtration and give presentations to the associated graded rings $\operatorname{gr}_{\gamma}K_0(\mathscr H_g)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Ruofan Zeng

item.title: Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.27517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a strong Hodge decomposition theorem for Novikov type Landau--Ginzburg models, that is, triples $(M,g,\theta)$ consisting of a non-compact complete K\"ahler manifold $(M,g)$ and a non-trivial closed holomorphic one-form $\theta$ on $M$.Under the well-tameness condition and under the assumption that $M$ is Stein, we prove that the space of $L^{2}$-forms on $M$ admits an orthogonal decomposition into the space of harmonic forms of the twisted Laplacian $\Delta_{\theta}$ and the images of the twisted Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial+\theta\wedge$ and $\bar\partial^{\dagger}+\iota_{\bar\theta^{\sharp}}$; moreover, the harmonic space is concentrated in degree $n=\dim_{\C}M$ and is isomorphic to the Milnor rings of $\theta$. As applications, we endow the complement of a hyperplane arrangement with a complete cylindrical K\"ahler metric, and we show that the differential of a master function with nonresonant weights is well-tamed with respect to this metric. After passing to a log resolution in the non-normal-crossing case; we then apply the results to the Yang--Yang functional of the Gaudin model, whose critical points are the Bethe roots: the top-degree harmonic space is described by the corresponding Milnor rings, and the number of Bethe roots is given by the Varchenko--Orlik--Terao lattice formula.
item.dc:creator: Huijun Fan, Jieran Wang

item.title: Secondary Chow Invariants beyond Lawson--Massey Products
item.description: arXiv:2610.27557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct secondary Chow invariants that cannot be recovered from Lawson--Massey realization. For every smooth complex projective curve $C$ of positive genus and every $n\ge2$, explicit cubical defining systems yield $n$ distinct Massey values in $\rm{CH}^{3}(C\times P^{2},1)$, with zero full indeterminacy, forming a cyclic group of order $n$. All corresponding triples have identical morphic classes and zero morphic, Lawson, and singular Massey brackets, despite nonzero target groups. The values are detected by the Weil pairing. We further construct secondary quotient classes of every finite order on smooth projective varieties with ample canonical bundle in every dimension at least two, and prove that generically finite pullbacks of coprime degree preserve their exact orders. These constructions obstruct integral and prime-local motivic formality, although the corresponding brackets become $\{0\}$ after reduction modulo every integer $m\ge2$. All specified values are torsion and vanish after rationalization.
item.dc:creator: Wenchuan Hu

item.title: Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veroneseans
item.description: arXiv:2610.27625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. We also show that many Terracini loci involve only sets with "intratangent pairs" that lie on the same tangent space to the underlying Veronese variety. Finally, we give some applications to algebraic statistics, showing that osculating varieties of Veronese varieties are moment varieties for local mixtures of location families and connecting Terracini loci to local identifiability.
item.dc:creator: Douglas A. Torrance

item.title: Nef complexity of klt Fano varieties: the full spectrum and classification below two
item.description: arXiv:2610.27676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a complex klt Fano variety. We study the rational total index $\tau_X$ and the nef complexity $c_X=\dim X+\rho(X)-\tau_X$. Previous joint work of the author with Enwright, Filipazzi, Gongyo, Moraga, Svaldi, and Wang established the corresponding nonnegativity and zero-case characterization in the broader framework of a special class of generalized log Calabi--Yau pairs. Here we give a direct proof in the Fano setting, prove that there is no value strictly between zero and one, and classify all klt Fano varieties with $c_X<2$, without assuming $\mathbb Q$-factoriality. At complexity one, after splitting off projective-space factors, the remaining factor is a normal quadric of Picard number one, a linear blow-up of projective space, or an integral $(1,1)$ hypersurface in a product of projective spaces. If $1<c_X<2$, only two weighted-projective families occur; in particular, no smooth Fano variety has nef complexity strictly between one and two. We also determine the spectrum when the dimension is allowed to vary: \[ \{0\}\cup\left\{2-\frac2q \ \middle| \ q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq2}\right\} \cup(\mathbb Q\cap[2,\infty)). \] Most proofs in this paper were developed from arguments generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT through discussions initiated and guided by the author; see the statement on the use of generative AI.
item.dc:creator: Kiwamu Watanabe

item.title: Lattice Moduli and Residual Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2610.27723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study prescribed holomorphic lattices for regular-singular connections and residual factors of quantum $F$-bundles. For an arbitrary ordered monodromy spectrum, we classify the fully framed local groupoid: each residue fibre is a discrete affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$, with a unique normal form and trivial stabilisers. We then analyse elementary changes of lattice. A strictly positive integral residue difference obstructs the oriented wall; otherwise, in arbitrary rank, the extending normal-form arcs form an affine torsor of relative dimension $r(r-1)$, and specialisation to the shifted residue slice is polynomial and triangular by root height. Adjacent walls exhibit the composite-root correction dictated by the type-$A$ root-subgroup relations, while an example over the dual numbers detects a nilpotent saturation defect. For one-branch $F$-bundles, the scalar branch is recovered from the residual trace, and scalar residualisation yields a symmetric monoidal equivalence with zero-branch $F$-bundles. This construction yields residual atoms, functorial Jordan strata, and a residual chemical formula compatible with blow-ups and projective bundles. In the $A$-model, residualisation removes the unit direction; the rationally marked large-radius residual germ recovers the divisor cubic and distinguishes the marked residual germs of the Pfaffian and Grassmannian Calabi--Yau threefolds.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Corr\^ea

item.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Dmitrii Pavlov, Rainer Sinn

item.title: Rational analytic prismatization
item.description: arXiv:2610.27918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory
item.dc:creator: Johannes Ansch\"utz, Arthur-C\'esar Le Bras, Juan Esteban Rodr\'iguez Camargo, Peter Scholze

item.title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
item.description: arXiv:2610.27934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Kydonakis, Lutian Zhao

item.title: Classification of SNC $(p,k)$-planes with Hodge structures of K3 type
item.description: arXiv:2610.27961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A SNC $(p,k)$-plane is a $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$-Galois cover $\pi\colon X \to \mathbb P^2$ with a simple normal crossing branch locus. In this setting, there exist several intermediate quotients $Y_1, Y_2,\dots, Y_{\phi_{p,k}}$ corresponding to subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$ of index $p$. We focus on the case where each $Y_i$ is either a surface with geometric genus $0$ or $1$, with at least one with geometric genus $1$. We classify all SNC $(p,k)$-planes satisfying these conditions obtaining that an extensive list of cases are minimal regular surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. Moreover, these assumptions allow us to have strong control over the weight-$2$ Hodge structure of the minimal model of the covering surface $X$. Therefore, we also prove that Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures hold for such surfaces. As an independent result of our methods, we obtain a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $1$, which turn out to be precisely all K3 surfaces, and a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $0$, which turn out to be instead rational surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Federico Fallucca, Matteo Penegini, Anna Ulivi

item.title: Harder-Narasimhan Filtrations of Hyperquiver Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperquiver representations are generalisations of quiver representations. They are directed hypergraphs with vector spaces assigned to vertices, and for every directed hyperedge, an assignment of a linear map from the tensor product of the source vector spaces to the tensor product of the target vector spaces. We study the moduli of hyperquiver representations, where we use affine GIT to describe the (in)stability of such objects under the action of a product of general linear groups. Our main result introduces the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of a hyperquiver representation. We also derive a formula for the weights of this unique filtration, which specialise to the Harder-Narasimhan slopes of a quiver representation.
item.dc:creator: Tommi Muller

item.title: Real Nullstellensatz for nilpotent Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.28113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a real Nullstellensatz for the universal enveloping algebra U(g) of a nilpotent finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g: An ideal of U(g) is real if and only if it is the intersection of kernels of irreducible integrable *-representations of U(g) by (in general unbounded) operators on a Hilbert space. For this, we build upon some classical results about the complexification of U(g) that lead to a complex Nullstellensatz (every semiprime ideal is the intersection of primitive ideals), but focus only on the ``real points'', i.e., the *-representations on Hilbert spaces. On the technical side, this requires to take into account an involution of U(g), namely, the antipode of its Hopf algebra structure, which goes into the definition of real ideals of U(g). Our result is the first noncommutative real Nullstellensatz for *-algebras with unbounded irreducible *-representations, demonstrating how methods of real algebraic geometry can lead to results about operator *-algebras also in situations where C*-algebraic methods fail.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Schmitt, Matthias Sch\"otz

item.title: Divisors on regular Hessenberg varieties for h=(2,3,4,...,n,n) associated to lower subsets
item.description: arXiv:2610.28114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a regular Hessenberg variety associated to the Hessenberg function $h=(2,3,4,\ldots,n,n)$, we construct Cartier divisors $D_A$ associated to lower subsets $\emptyset\subsetneq A\subsetneq[n]$. We show that their first Chern classes satisfy the quadratic relations suggested by the combination of the works of B$\breve{\text{a}}$libanu-Crooks and Horiguchi-Masuda-Shareshian-Song. We also give a characterization of these divisors in terms of the centralizer action. It also follows that these divisors generate the (pseudo)effective cone of divisors on the Hessenberg variety.
item.dc:creator: Hiraku Abe, Haozhi Zeng

item.title: There are no Miyaoka--Kobayashi octics
item.description: arXiv:2610.28135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $n$ with only ADE singularities. Using K\"ahler-Einstein metrics, Kobayashi proved an upper bound, in terms of $n$, for a sum of local invariants of the singular points of $C$. For even $n$ this bound had been obtained earlier by Hirzebruch and Ivinskis. Curves of even degree for which equality holds are called Miyaoka-Kobayashi curves, and the only known examples are three types of plane sextics. We show that there are no Miyaoka--Kobayashi curves of degree $8$, and additionally that a Miyaoka-Kobayashi curve of degree $10$ cannot be free. The key new ingredient is a new linear constraint on the singularities of such curves, obtained by differentiating Langer's orbifold Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau inequality.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora

item.title: The stacky approach to de Rham-Witt cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2610.28149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. Ekedahl proved an equivalence of triangulated categories between bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring and complexes of $F$-gauges. We give a geometric proof, independent of his proof, that the de Rham-Witt realization is a symmetric monoidal equivalence of stable $\infty$-categories between perfect $F$-gauges and bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring with Ekedahl's completed star product, as expected by Illusie. The geometry comes from topological restriction homology: $\mathrm{TR}^r(k;\mathbf Z_p)^{hS^1}$ is an iterated fibre product of copies of $\mathrm{TC}^-(k;\mathbf Z_p)$, and taking even stacks before and after the fibre product gives the genuine and the naive $r$-Nygaard stacks. Pushforward from the genuine to the naive $r$-Nygaard stack realizes Andriopoulos' $r$-Nygaard filtrations, which interpolate between the Nygaard filtration at $r=1$ and the Hodge-Witt filtration at $r=\infty$. On the genuine $r$-Nygaard stack, which is a chain of Nygaard charts, restriction and Frobenius come from the inclusions of sub-chains, Verschiebung from duality, and the differential as a Bockstein operator, and the relations of the star product become projection formulas. As applications, we deduce Ekedahl's K\"unneth formula and Poincar\'e duality for de Rham-Witt cohomology from their counterparts for $F$-gauge cohomology, and show that the special-value formulas of Illusie and of Mondal over finite fields are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Yuanning Zhang

item.title: A Twisted bidifferential, second fundamental form of Prym map and projective structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.28156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a point $[(\widetilde{C},C)]$ of the moduli space ${\mathcal R}_g$, where $\widetilde{C}$ is an \'etale double cover of a smooth curve $C$ of genus $g \,\geq\, 7$, we construct a twisted meromorphic bidifferential $\widehat{\eta}_P$ on $C\times C$ with a pole on the diagonal. It is shown that the second fundamental form $\rho_P$ of the Prym map from ${\mathcal R}_g$ to ${\mathcal A}_{g-1}$ at $[(\widetilde{C},C)]$ is given by this $\widehat{\eta}_P$. This allows us to compare $\rho_P$ with the second fundamental forms of the two Torelli maps, to ${\mathcal A}_{2g-1}$ and ${\mathcal A}_{g}$, at the points $[\widetilde{C}]$ and $[C]$ respectively. It is shown that $\widehat{\eta}_P$ induces a projective structure on $C$ that depends on the double cover $\widetilde{C}\, \longrightarrow\, C$; these projective structures together give a ${\mathcal C}^{\infty}$ section $\beta_P$ of the bundle of projective structures on the moduli space ${\mathcal R}_g$. Finally, it is proved that the $(0,\,1)$-component of the differential of the section $\beta_P$ is the pullback of the K\"ahler form of the Siegel metric on ${\mathcal A}_{g-1}$ via the Prym map. This is a key ingredient in the proof that this section $\beta_P$ is not the pullback of a section of projective structures on ${\mathcal M}_{g}$ and, in addition, that it differs from the known projective structures on ${\mathcal R}_g$.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Elisabetta Colombo, Paola Frediani, Alessandro Ghigi

item.title: Twisted group codes of dimension 2 and 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.28297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that all group codes of dimension at most $3$ are permutation equivalent to abelian group codes. We prove that twisted group codes of dimension at most $3$ are monomially equivalent either to an abelian group code or to an irreducible constacyclic code, and in the second case we describe the code explicitly by means of a trace map. Monomial equivalence cannot be replaced by permutation equivalence, and the second case cannot be avoided: the ternary tetracode is an ideal of $\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^4+1)$ but it is not monomially equivalent to any group code. More generally, we give two infinite families, in dimensions $2$ and $3$, of irreducible constacyclic codes which attain the Griesmer bound, whereas every group code with the same length and dimension has smaller minimum distance.
item.dc:creator: Alvaro Otero Sanchez

item.title: Convergence and semisimplicity of big quantum cohomology of flag varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.28418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture that the big quantum cohomology of a flag variety $G/P$ of general Lie type is convergent near the large-radius limit and is generically semisimple. The convergence relies on a slightly modified version of Iritani's reconstruction theorem, together with Cauchy's formula that avoids directly taking the non-equivariant limit at the origin. Generic semisimplicity follows from a surprising application of the big quantum $D$-module mirror symmetry for $G/P$ established by the first, third and fourth authors jointly with Hinault and Zhang. Moreover, we prove the regularity conjecture on the big quantum cohomology of $G/P$ formulated by Perrin and Smirnov, which implies generic semisimplicity.
item.dc:creator: Changzheng Li, Zhaoyang Liu, Tony Yue Yu, Chi Zhang

item.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.28456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.
item.dc:creator: Jagadish Pine

item.title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
item.description: arXiv:2610.28464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $\Omega^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.
item.dc:creator: Jagadish Pine

item.title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.28499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Massri

item.title: Higher-order tangent lines to smooth hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every smooth hypersurface $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d\geq n \geq 5$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the space of pointed lines $(\ell,p)$ having intersection multiplicity at least six with $X$ at $p$ has the expected dimension $2n-7$. The proof uses deformations of ruled surfaces preserving prescribed contact with $X$. As an application, we show that a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\geq 6$ in $\mathbb{P}^5$ contains at most $225d^3-1370d^2+1800d$ planes. This bound has optimal order of growth in $d$.
item.dc:creator: Roya Beheshti, Shibashis Mukhopadhyay

item.title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.
item.dc:creator: Paul Balavoine, Severin L\"ust

item.title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.27392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.
item.dc:creator: Xu Zhuang

item.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.27554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Reed, Manolis C. Tsakiris

item.title: A new class of smooth algebraic varieties with the density property and a counterexample to the T\'{o}th-Varolin Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the smooth affine hypersurfaces \[ X_{m,n}=\{\zeta^mz_0^n+ (1+z_1\zeta)z_2+\zeta z_3^2=1\}\subset\mathbb{C}^5,\;\; m,n\geq 2, \] have the density property. For every odd integer $d\geq 3$, we identify $X_{d-1,d}$ with a Kaliman modification along a Brieskorn variety of type $(d,2,2,2)$. We prove that the fourfolds $X_{d-1,d}$ are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$ but not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$. These, therefore, give counterexamples to the T\'{o}th-Varolin conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Sushil Gorai

item.title: Fourier Decomposition and E-Eigenvalues of Hypergraph Polynomials over Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with polynomial $f_H(\bm{x})=\sum_{e\in E}\prod_{v\in e}x_v$. For a finite abelian group $G$ and a subgroup $S$ of $G$, the $k$-partite Cayley hypergraph $K$ has $k$ disjoint vertex parts, each indexed by $G$, and $\{(1,g_1),\ldots,(k,g_k)\}$ is an edge if and only if $g_1+\cdots+g_k\in S$. For $k=2$, $K$ is isomorphic to the Bi-Cayley graph associated with $G$ and $S$. For $k\ge3$, we use character theory to express $f_K$, under a complex unitary change of variables, as a sum of exactly $[G:S]$ nonzero monomials in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. This yields a direct sum decomposition whenever $S$ is a proper subgroup of $G$. When $G=\Z_2^m$, this transformation is real and orthogonal, enabling us to determine the complete sets of complex E-eigenvalues and Z-eigenvalues of the adjacency tensor of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Yan-Hong Bao, Yi-Zheng Fan, Lili Liao

item.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits\ for Positive Factorial Multiples
item.description: arXiv:2610.28338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ \tau(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Liang Zhang (Michael), Xiaohua (Michael), Xuan

item.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
item.description: arXiv:2610.28439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Alvaro Ribot, Yulia Alexandr, Anna Seigal

item.title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
item.description: arXiv:2610.28497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\deg d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Anton Selemenchuk

item.title: Generic finiteness of solutions to parametrized systems of generalized polynomial inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.28588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study parametrized systems of $\mathit{generalized}$ polynomial inequalities, $(c \circ x^B) \in C$, for a positive variable vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n_>$, a $\mathit{real}$ exponent matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, a positive parameter vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m_>$, and a positive, blunt coefficient cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^m_>$. This setting includes (i) generalized polynomial equations, $A \, (c \circ x^B) = 0$, arising e.g. from power-law dynamical systems with real exponents (and involving a real coefficient matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n' \times m}$), and (ii) generalized semi-algebraic sets. Our main result guarantees the generic finiteness of solutions modulo unavoidable exponential fibers. Building on a framework for parametrized $\mathit{polynomial}$ systems developed by M\"uller and Regensburger, we reformulate the problem as a system of $\mathit{binomial}$ equations on the coefficient set $P = C \cap \Delta \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m_>$, where $\Delta$ is a product of (standard) simplices. Solvability is governed by the monomial-dependency subspace $D$. Using elementary arguments from analysis and topology, including a logarithmic boundary analysis and Sard's theorem, we control the accumulation of solutions on the boundary and in the interior of $P$. We show that, if $\dim P \le \dim D$, then generically in both the measure-theoretic and topological sense, there are finitely many solutions on $P$ (and hence finitely many exponential fibers of solutions in $\mathbb{R}^n_>$). As an application, we prove generic finiteness of steady states (within forward-invariant sets) for parametrized power-law dynamical systems with real exponents.
item.dc:creator: Stefan M\"uller

item.title: Apollonian carpets and the boundary of the Kahler cone of a hyperkahler manifold
item.description: arXiv:2402.11697v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ample cone of a compact Kahler $n$-manifold $M$ is the intersection of its Kahler cone and the real subspace generated by integer (1,1)-classes. Its isotropic boundary is the set of all points $\eta$ on its boundary such that $\int_M \eta^n=0$. We are interested in the relation between the shape of the isotropic boundary of the ample cone of a hyperkahler manifold and the dynamics of its holomorphic automorphism group $G$. In this case, the projectivization of the ample cone is realized as an open, locally polyhedral subset in a hyperbolic space $H$. The isotropic boundary $S$ is realized as a subset of the hyperbolic boundary (the absolute) $A$ of $H$, which is naturally identified with a Euclidean sphere. It is clear that the isotropic boundary $S$ contains the limit set of $G$ acting on its ample cone. We prove that, conversely, all irrational points on $S$ belong to the limit set. Using a result of N. Shah about limiting distributions of curves under geodesic flow on hyperbolic manifolds, we prove that every real analytic curve in $S$ is contained in a geodesic sphere in $S$,and in presence of such curves the limit set is the closure of the union of these geodesic spheres. We study the geometry of such fractal sets, called Apollonian carpets, and establish the link between the Apollonian carpet and the structure of the automorphism group.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina Amerik, Andrey Soldatenkov, Misha Verbitsky

item.title: Revisiting Gamma conjecture I: counterexamples and modifications
item.description: arXiv:2405.16979v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We continue investigation of asymptotics of quantum differential equation for Fano manifolds, with a special regard to Gamma conjecture I and its underlying Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$. We introduce the A-model conifold value, a symplectic invariant of a Fano manifold, and propose modifications for Gamma conjecture I based on this new definition. We discuss an interplay of birational transformations with an extension of Gamma conjecture I over the K\"ahler moduli space. These heuristics are applied to rigorously identify the principal asymptotic class in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles $X_n=\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^{n}}(\mathcal{O}\oplus\mathcal{O}(n))$. We observe, in particular, that for $X_n$ of dimension at least four, the Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$ holds just for even values of $n$, and in these cases we falsify the original non-modified Gamma conjecture I.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Galkin, Jianxun Hu, Hiroshi Iritani, Huazhong Ke, Changzheng Li, Zhitong Su

item.title: Equivariant aspects of de-completing cyclic homology
item.description: arXiv:2410.05994v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Derived de Rham cohomology turns out to be important in $p$-adic geometry, following Bhatt's discovery [Bha12] of conjugate filtration in char $p$, de-Hodge-completing results in [Bei12]. In [Kal18], Kaledin introduced an analogous de-completion of the periodic cyclic homology, called the polynomial periodic cyclic homology, equipped with a conjugate filtration in char $p$, and expected to be related to derived de Rham cohomology. In this article, using genuine equivariant homotopy structure on Hochschild homology as in [ABG+18, BHM22], we give an equivariant description of Kaledin's polynomial periodic cyclic homology. This leads to Morita invariance without any Noetherianness assumption as in [Kal18], and the comparison to derived de Rham cohomology becomes transparent. Moreover, this description adapts directly to "topological" analogues, which gives rise to a de-Nygaard-completion of the topological periodic cyclic homology, which admits an extension to linear categories over truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. As an application, we establish a noncommutative crystalline--de Rham comparison, which decompletes the result in [PV19], and extends it to prime $p=2$. We also compare polynomial periodic cyclic homology to topological Hochschild homology over $\mathbb F_p$, and produce a conjugate filtration in char p from our description.
item.dc:creator: Zhouhang Mao

item.title: The Chow Ring of the 2-Sylow Subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(4,2)$
item.description: arXiv:2506.06512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a computation of the mod 2 Chow ring of the motivic \'etale classifying space of the finite group $\mathrm{Syl}_2(\mathrm{GL}(4,2))$. It outlines a general computation strategy, adapted from work by Burt Totaro, that has been largely automated by the author. This strategy can be used to compute more examples of Chow rings of motivic \'etale classifying spaces quickly.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Ziegler

item.title: Modeling Group Actions on Stacks (Especially the Lubin-Tate Action)
item.description: arXiv:2507.00309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose we are given a profinite group G acting on a formal moduli stack M, and we want to understand the group action, and compute cohomology related to this group action. How can we do it? This prolegomenon conveys two methods of pinning down such an action: geometric modeling and the two-tower method. We highlight their use on a specific action -- the automorphisms of a formal group acting on its deformation space, called the Lubin-Tate action. We provide the toolkit that these two methods run on. The pieces of the kit are standard in their own subjects, but the Lubin-Tate action requires us to sew them together and ask more of them than their usual statements give, and several are set down here in that stronger form: equivariantly, in families, and with the grading kept. The tools are put to work in the two sequels, which build geometric models at height p-1 and at the heights p^{k-1}(p-1) above it; the two-tower material is a companion to the proof of the coheight one weak chromatic splitting conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Rin Ray

item.title: Infinitesimal Torelli problems for special Gushel-Mukai and related Fano threefolds: Hodge theoretical and categorical perspectives
item.description: arXiv:2507.06995v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A hyperelliptic curve is the classical example of a variety for which the global Torelli theorem holds while the differential of the period map has a kernel, forced by the extra involution. We study the analogous phenomenon for Fano threefolds that are double covers of rigid Fano threefolds branched along a K3 surface, mainly special Gushel--Mukai threefolds. We prove that the part of the infinitesimal period map invariant under the covering involution is injective, so that the kernel is exactly the three-dimensional space of anti-invariant deformations, one more than for ordinary Gushel--Mukai threefolds. We give a Hodge-theoretic proof, which reduces to a twisted infinitesimal Torelli theorem for the branch K3 surface, and a categorical proof, based on Kuznetsov's normal Hochschild cohomology, which also applies in genus eight and identifies the kernel with the tangent space to a distinguished point of a Bridgeland moduli space. The two descriptions of the kernel are related directly through the Pl\"ucker net and the conic of special lines of the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Finally, ordinary Verra threefolds satisfy the infinitesimal Torelli theorem, while special ones have a one-dimensional kernel; in both cases the kernel agrees with that of the categorical period map of a Clifford component, and it is the tangent space to the deformations of a canonical spinor bundle, which is rigid in the ordinary case and obstructed at second order in the special case.
item.dc:creator: Xun Lin, Shizhuo Zhang, Zheng Zhang

item.title: Relative mirror symmetry, theta functions and the Gamma conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2508.06750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a Fano variety, and $D\subset X$ be an snc anticanonical divisor. We study relative mirror symmetry for the log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,D)$. (1) We prove a relative mirror theorem for snc pairs without assuming the divisors are nef. (2) We study theta functions associated with the pair $(X,D)$. (3) We introduce functions on the mirror that are obtained from the higher-degree part of the big relative quantum cohomology. As an application, we use these new ingredients in relative mirror symmetry to prove a version of the mirror symmetric Gamma conjecture for $X$ for $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{pt}}$ in this setting, where the Landau--Ginzburg potential is defined as a sum of theta functions.
item.dc:creator: Fenglong You

item.title: Descent problem for certificate of non-negativity on semi-algebraic sets
item.description: arXiv:2508.07060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a subfield of $\mathbb R$ and let $K$ be a basic closed semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb R$ with $\partial K\subset F$. Let $\mathcal N$ be the natural choice of generators of $K$. We show that if $f\in F[x]$ is $\geq 0$ on $K$, then $f$ can be written as $$f=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^s } a_e\sigma_e g^e $$ where $a_e\in F_{\geq 0}$, $\sigma_e\in \sum F[x]^2$ and $g^{e}=g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_s^{e_s}$. In other words, the preordering $T_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated. In case $F=\mathbb R$, this result is due to Kuhlmann and Marshall. As an application, we prove that if $K$ is compact, then $M_{\mathcal N}=T_{\mathcal N}=Pos(K)$. In other words, the quadratic module $M_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated.
item.dc:creator: Manoj K. Keshari, Debapriya Ojha, Niladri Sekhar Patra

item.title: A cluster criterion for potential degeneracy of superelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2508.15974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a field with a discrete valuation; let $p$ be a prime; and let $C$ be the curve defined by an equation of the form $y^p = f(x)$. We show that the curve $C$ has a model over an algebraic extension of $K$ whose special fiber consists of genus-$0$ components and has at worst nodal singularities if and only if the cluster data of the roots of $f$ satisfies a certain criterion, and when these hold, we show explicitly how to build the minimal regular model of $C$. We develop an interpretation of cluster data in terms of a convex hull in the Berkovich projective line and express the above results directly in terms of this convex hull.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Yelton

item.title: Non-degenerate mixed maps and contact structures
item.description: arXiv:2510.03033v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theory of mixed isolated complete intersection singularities: real analytic maps $(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C^k,0)$ in the variables $z$ and $\bar z$ that are submersions along their punctured zero fiber. We give a Newton non-degeneracy criterion for this property and three sources of examples: Siegel maps arising from linear actions, mixed coverings, and mixed Hamm maps. For maps built from blocks of polar degree one that satisfy a weighted positivity condition, the punctured zero fiber is symplectic and every spherical link is contact, with the polar action as Reeb flow. Conversely, contact links of polar weighted maps force symplectic zero fibers, whereas the zero fibers of Siegel maps are coisotropic. Along the deformation of a mixed Hamm map to its holomorphic counterpart we prove exact symplectic rigidity: the punctured zero fibers are identified by equivariant maps that preserve the weighted Liouville form, the radius and every coordinate stratum. Hence all their links are strictly contactomorphic to the holomorphic Hamm link with its canonical contact structure, and the strict contact type depends only on the polar exponents and the dimensions. At each fixed radius these identifications extend to contact isotopies of the ambient weighted sphere. We also construct adapted open books, show that the ambient open books of mixed Hamm functions support the standard contact sphere, and deduce positive-stabilization equivalence in dimension three from Giroux's correspondence. Finally, we prove contact stability under higher-order perturbations of a radially homogeneous principal part.
item.dc:creator: In\'acio Rabelo, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: Cartier duality for gerbes of vector bundles
item.description: arXiv:2512.24967v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Cartier duality for gerbes of algebraic and analytic vector bundles as an anti-equivalence of Hopf algebras in the category of kernels of analytic stacks. As an application, we prove that the category of solid quasi-coherent sheaves on the Hodge-Tate stack of a smooth rigid variety over an algebraically closed field $C$ of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ is equivalent to the category of weight $1$ sheaves on Bhatt-Zhang's Simpson gerbe.
item.dc:creator: Juan Esteban Rodr\'iguez Camargo

item.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
item.description: arXiv:2604.06979v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Demarche

item.title: Equisingularity in families of double point curves
item.description: arXiv:2605.08507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide a systematic comparison between the equisingularity of a 1-parameter unfolding $F = (f_t, t)$ of a finitely determined map germ $f: (\mathbb{C}^2, 0) \to (\mathbb{C}^3, 0)$ and the equisingularity of its associated families of double point curves: $D(F)$, $F(D(F))$, $D^2(F)$, and $D^2(F)/S_2$. We also construct explicit counterexamples to several natural questions concerning the equisingularity of these loci. As a key application, we introduce new families of complete intersection curves -- referred to as Henry--type families -- which are topologically trivial but fail to satisfy the Whitney equisingularity conditions. Finally, we generalize classical formulas for double point curves, originally established for map germs from $(\mathbb{C}^2, 0)$ to $(\mathbb{C}^3, 0)$, to the higher-dimensional setting of map germs from $(\mathbb{C}^n, 0)$ to $(\mathbb{C}^{2n-1}, 0)$ for $n \geq 3$, thereby endowing the associated curves with a convenient analytic structure.
item.dc:creator: Otoniel Nogueira da Silva, Manoel Messias da Silva J\'unior

item.title: A solution to the Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture through Special Fujita Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2605.30063v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that any big line bundle on a smooth projective variety admits a special Fujita approximation: the volume and the first Riemann-Roch coefficient are both approximated by those of ample $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundles on higher models. Exploiting previous works by Boucksom, Jonsson and Li, we solve the Boucksom-Jonsson Regularization Conjecture on the Non-Archimedean entropy functional. As a main consequence, we obtain a solution to the (uniform version of the) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture: a polarized smooth projective variety $(X,L)$ admits a cscK metric if and only if it is $\mathrm{Aut}^\circ(X,L)$-uniformly $K$-stable. This extends the known Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for smooth Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Trusiani

item.title: A complete curve of genus 5 in the moduli space of curves of genus 3 and related questions
item.description: arXiv:2607.13486v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let M_3 be the coarse moduli space of smooth complex projective curves of genus 3. Through a general point of M_3, we construct a smooth complete curve of genus 21 and gonality 7, and a singular complete curve whose normalization has genus 19 and gonality 6. We also construct a Hodge-generic complete trigonal curve of geometric genus 5 in M_3.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Grushevsky, Christophe Ritzenthaler

item.title: Finite Group Reduction of the DR/DZ Hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2607.16607v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the finite group reduction of the Dubrovin-Zhang/Double Ramification hierarchy associated with a semisimple CohFT preserves its bihamiltonian structure and its tau structure. By applying this result to the orbifold Gromov-Witten theory with the target $\mathbb{P}^1_{2,2,2,2}$, we obtain two non-equivalent integrable hierarchies which can be associated with the Frobenius manifold structure on the Hurwitz space $M_{1;1}$, and we show that one of them is equivalent to the genus one topological recursion.
item.dc:creator: Si-Qi Liu, Youjin Zhang, Tianwen Zhong

item.title: Point Counts of Cluster Varieties of Marked Surfaces Over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2608.22208v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish formulae for point counts of cluster varieties of cluster algebras of marked surfaces, possibly with punctures. We then establish formulae for the number of non-deep points in these cluster varieties over $\mathbb{F}_2$, which gives us the number of algebraic tori necessary to cover the cluster manifold over $\mathbb{F}_2$. We also show that these formulae satisfy certain recurrence relations.
item.dc:creator: James Beyer

item.title: A classification of zero $p$-rank curves with large automorphism groups in odd characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2609.33185v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\cX$ be a curve of genus $g\ge2$ and $p$-rank zero over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $G\le\Aut(\cX)$ satisfy $|G|>24g(g-1)$. We prove that $G$ fixes a point unless $(\cX,G)$ belongs to an explicit list. For $g\ge4$, the curve is a cyclic quotient of a Hermitian curve, of a Giulietti--Korchm\'aros curve, or of Skabelund's cover of a Ree curve. We determine the equations and all the groups $G$ that occur, including their central kernels. The exceptional $A_7$ action in characteristic $5$ is on the Hermitian curve of degree $6$; genera $2$ and $3$ are treated separately. The equations are recovered from the group action by two rigidity lemmas for equivariant one-point $p$-group covers of the affine line. If $G$ has no common fixed point and its Sylow $p$-subgroups are noncyclic, then, unless $G$ induces ${}^2G_2(3)$ on the orbit of Sylow fixed points, the bound $|G|>\max\{84(g-1),2g^2\}$ gives a rational quotient with exactly one wild and one tame short orbit, and a rational Sylow quotient.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian

item.title: Failure of local extension of semipositive metrics in a smooth projective family
item.description: arXiv:2609.36410v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a smooth projective family of rational surfaces and an effective line bundle on its total space that give a negative answer to P\u{a}un's metric-extension question. The restricted bundle on the central fibre carries a semipositively curved singular Hermitian metric with analytic and minimal singularities, but this metric admits no semipositive extension to any neighbourhood of the whole fibre, even up to singularity type. The construction uses four-point blow-ups of the plane, with three centres becoming collinear on the central fibre. This change produces a nonzero integrable adjoint section on the central fibre, whereas the corresponding adjoint systems vanish on nearby noncentral fibres. If a metric extension existed, an $L^2$ extension theorem would extend that section, contradicting this vanishing.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: Supersingular Tate conjecture for irreducible symplectic varieties of known types: I
item.description:
arXiv:2609.38801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for a supersingular irreducible symplectic variety admitting suitable lifting to characteristic zero has Tate Chow motive if it is of deformation type $K3^{[n]}$, OG6 (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 4), or OG10 (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 12), and has supersingular abelian Chow motive if it is of $\mathrm{Kum}^n$-type (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 3). In particular, any product of those irreducible symplectic varieties satisfies the supersingular Tate conjecture for the whole $\ell$-adic or crystalline cohomology ring.
item.dc:creator: Lie Fu, Xuanlin Huang, Zhiyuan Li

item.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.16350v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products. As a consequence, when $g\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, $T_{n,L}$ satisfies property $(N_p)$ for $\mathrm{deg}(L)\geq(n+1)g+p$. This bound is sharp for elliptic symmetric squares and also gives evidence for a folklore conjecture on adjoint syzygies.
item.dc:creator: Wenbo Niu, Peter Yi Wei

item.title: Remarks on Lattice Actions Corresponding to Automorphism Groups of Smooth Cubic Fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19161v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The automorphism groups of smooth cubic fourfolds over the complex numbers, together with actions on defining equations, are classified in previous works. In this paper, we complete the calculation of group actions on the primitive integral cohomology lattice for all of the $156$ families in the classification. We distinguish similar families, determine the remaining action-maximal cases, and use restriction to complete the list. We also determine the generic algebraic lattices for each family. The calculation depends mainly on OSCAR.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fu

item.title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20239v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\operatorname{SP}^{d}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the $d$-th symmetric product of complex projective space. We prove that its integral cycle class map is split injective and has finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$. We also compute the ranks of its Chow groups. By constructing compatible integral retractions on Chow groups and singular homology, we prove that addition of a fixed point induces an isomorphism on the Chow group of $q$-dimensional cycles whenever $d\geq q$. For $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq 6$, we construct a nonalgebraic class of order two in codimension two. Its image generates a direct summand of the cycle class cokernel and remains nonalgebraic after addition of fixed points. Consequently, integral surjectivity fails both at certain finite stages with $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product. We further identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology of the smooth configuration space. Finally, we provide an example where multiplication by an even integer annihilates a nonzero Chow class of order two.
item.dc:creator: Youming Chen, Wenchuan Hu

item.title: The theory of F-rational signature
item.description: arXiv:1911.02642v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: F-signature is an important numeric invariant of singularities in positive characteristic that can be used to detect strong F-regularity. One would like to have a variant that rather detects F-rationality, and there are two theories that aim to fill this gap: F-rational signature of Hochster and Yao and dual F-signature of Sannai. Unfortunately, several important properties of the original F-signature are unknown for these invariants. We give a modification of the Hochster-Yao definition that agrees with Sannai's dual F-signature and push further the united theory to achieve a complete generalization of F-signature.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Smirnov, Kevin Tucker

item.title: Superconnections and Bott-Chern valued Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck for complex orbifolds, I
item.description: arXiv:2505.13912v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use flat antiholomorphic superconnections to study orbifold Chern character following the method introduced by Bismut, Shen, and Wei on general complex orbifolds. We show the uniqueness of orbifold Chern character by proving a Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck theorem for orbifold embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Qiaochu Ma, Xiang Tang, Hsian-Hua Tseng, Zhaoting Wei

item.title: Extremal monomials of $q$-characters
item.description: arXiv:2510.08103v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this short paper, we prove a conjecture of Frenkel-Hernandez, which states that $q$-characters of finite-dimensional simple modules of the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}})$ are bounded by the Weyl group orbit of the leading monomial under Chari's braid group action. This can be regarded as a (partial) quantum affine generalization of the Weyl group invariance of characters of finite-dimensional representations of $\mathfrak{g}$.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Negu\c{t}

item.title: Properties of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.10818v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We continue the study of compact holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds $X$ that we introduced recently by expanding the discussion to include non-K\"ahler hyperbolicity issues and a differential calculus based on what we call the Lie derivative with respect to a $(0,\,q)$-form with values in the holomorphic tangent bundle of $X$. We also propose the notion of $p$-contact deformations for which we prove a Bogomolov-Tian-Todorov-type unobstructedness theorem to order two. This kind of small deformations of the complex structure is related to the essential horizontal deformations that we introduced in our previous work and forms part of a wider on-going project aimed at developing a non-K\"ahler mirror symmetry theory that was first tested on the Iwasawa manifold and subsequently on Calabi-Yau page-$1$-$\partial\bar\partial$-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Hisashi Kasuya, Dan Popovici, Luis Ugarte

item.title: Quantization in polarization via transverse Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
item.description: arXiv:2512.15060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct, for every prequantizable symplectic manifold $(M,\omega,L)$ equipped with a nonsingular polarization, a deformation quantization $(C_M^\infty[[\hbar]],\star)$ together with a filtered sheaf of subalgebras $C_{M,\hbar}^{(<\infty)}$ that admits an exact action on polarized sections of $L^{\otimes k}$ for each $k\in\mathbb Z^+$. This extends the Kostant--Souriau action of polarization-preserving functions. The main geometric ingredient is a transverse PBW theory associated with a Nirenberg integrable distribution $P$. For any locally free $P$-modules $E$ and $E'$, we construct a PBW isomorphism for the bundle of transverse differential operators from $E$ to $E'$. This extends the PBW theorem for Lie pairs of Laurent-Gengoux--Sti\'enon--Xu to the setting of $P$-modules. After specializing $\hbar= \tfrac{\sqrt{-1}}{k}$, we obtain a sheaf $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ of level-$k$ quantizable functions and prove that its action identifies $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ with the sheaf of transverse differential operators on $L^{\otimes k}$. In the K\"ahler case, this recovers the construction of Chan--Leung--Li. Finally, for standard symplectic tori with real polarizations, we compare our construction with Toeplitz-type operators and obtain their semiclassical asymptotic expansions.
item.dc:creator: Dan Wang, Yutung Yau

item.title: A Littlewood-Richardson Rule for Forest Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2606.23876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The forest polynomials $\mathfrak{P}_a$ of Nadeau-Tewari form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$ whose role for the cohomology of the quasisymmetric flag variety parallels that of Schubert polynomials for the classical flag variety. Nonnegativity of the structure constants $\beta_{a,b}^c$ in $\mathfrak{P}_a \mathfrak{P}_b = \sum_c \beta_{a,b}^c \mathfrak{P}_c$ is known, but no Littlewood-Richardson-style enumerative rule has been available. We give such a rule: $\beta_{a,b}^c$ counts pairs of forest RC graphs of forest-codes $a$ and $b$ whose lift product lands on a forest RC graph of forest-code and weight both equal to $c$. The same rule descends to the cup product on $H^\bullet(\mathrm{QFl}_n)$. The proof introduces a squash product $\boxtimes$ on RC graphs, which on full Grassmannian RC graphs of a fixed height recovers the plactic monoid, a multiplactic algebra $\mathcal{M}_n$ that models Schubert polynomial multiplication, and a lift product $*$ on RC graphs whose quasi-crystal structure, in the framework of Cain-Guilherme-Malheiro, transports the Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence through the computation. The row-decomposition machinery on RC graphs that underlies these constructions is developed in a companion paper.
